text:
emma: New hire hit a weird case: they unzipped redwoodctl to a folder on a WSL-mounted drive and `redwoodctl login` finished in the browser but CLI remained unauthenticated.
nirav: hmm. was the binary run from a symlink or from /mnt/c/... path?
emma: symlink in /usr/local/bin that pointed to /mnt/c/Users/guest/Downloads/redwoodctl.exe.
liz: ah, symlink + mount permissions can make the CLI write profile files to an unexpected location (sometimes the mount user is different). What does `redwoodctl profiles list --json` show?
emma: shows default -> /home/guest/.redwood and a second profile default-wsl -> /mnt/c/Users/guest/AppData/Local/Temp/rwd-999. Token was in the latter.
sam: summary: running from a mounted Windows path created an ephemeral profile on the Windows side. Browser callback wrote token there. After closing terminal, token gone.
nirav: fix strategy: 1) detect when binary path is on a foreign mount or under Temp and print a banner: "Running from a temporary or foreign mount; move binary to a native location or use the packaged installer." 2) add `redwoodctl doctor` that reports active profile path and binary path. 3) add `redwoodctl migrate --from <path> --to default` helper that copies tokens securely and removes the temp copy.
liz: add a short Quickstart blurb about not using symlinks to cross OS mounts for login flows and prefer native install. Also include a troubleshooting snippet: how to check profiles and migrate.
emma: QA notes: repro steps: create symlink in WSL to a Windows-extracted binary, run login, finish browser auth, then verify profiles. Add test matrix for symlinked installs on mac/linux and WSL mounts.
sam: I'll add unit to normalize and resolve symlinks when returning profile paths in `profiles list`. Also ensure migrate is atomic.
support-bot: support ticket created: DX-11021; include reproduction steps and recommended migrate command.
nirav: I'll push the banner + doctor command today; migrate helper and tests this sprint.
liz: small UX ask: if we detect a temp/foreign profile right after login, show an inline prompt: "Migrate token to persistent profile? (Y/n)" so non-technical new hires don't get stuck.
nirav: agree but keep it opt-in for safety. Noninteractive runs will prefer persistent dir.
emma: thanks all — this blocked a new hire for an hour, glad we have a clear path forward. :raised_hands:
